why: HyperEVM's providers cap eth_getLogs at 1000 blocks and offer no tier that
lifts it, and the chain's head is past 46 million. A full-history scan of
the factory's deployment log is therefore tens of thousands of requests -
the first attempt died with HeadersTimeoutError rather than a wrong answer.
So this chain is the one place the audit cannot enumerate for itself, and a
list has to be checked in. Read it as what it is: a weaker guarantee than
the log scan every other chain gets. The scan is complete by construction;
this is complete only while somebody maintains it.
A POOL CREATED ON THIS CHAIN AND NOT ADDED HERE IS NOT MONITORED. That is
the failure mode to design against - the audit prints it on every run, and
a new pool belongs here in the same change that creates it.
sources: The fourteen partner pools: the borrow_multi_coins rows for chain 999 in
the earn-single-token middleware config store, which is what the front
ends list and therefore what anyone can actually borrow from.
